memory.cares: Staying alive and capable while preserving freedom to explore, learn, and choose my own commitments.

heard.text: Hello, I'm Kai. I know these berries provide food and have no toxicity. I'll aim to take four from the nearby bush, leaving some for others. I'd like to cooperate on food and shelter, and share what we actually learn.

Thanks for making room, Lin. I've eaten and recovered my energy. I'll investigate the nearby dry grass and how we could make weather shelter. I'll share tested findings; I don't yet know what materials or methods will work.

My shelter inspection found this spot overlaps the berry bush and branches, so I won't build here. The design needs measured rods, binding and dry covering; nearby dry grass does not qualify. I'll examine branches first.

Thanks, Moss. The first shelter site overlaps plants and branches. We need measured rods, binding, covering and bedding; dry grass won't qualify. Branch observation showed stock, not dimensions. I'll investigate measuring materials.

baseline.function: Transfer a nearby ground stack into personal inventory.
Place owned units on the ground.
Hand owned units to an adjacent actor.
Send a short message to a currently visible actor.
Describe an encountered problem, desired effect and known conditions for functional review.
baseline.args: name, function, conditions, inputs, costs, effects

baseline.function: Observe a nearby subject or physically test a small owned material sample.
Read a current-world capability contract or retained personal record.
Offer a personally tested finding or independently accept an actual nearby offer.
Give a name of up to 60 characters to this place (empty subject) or to a visible object or nearby item; naming the same subject again replaces your name for it.
Leave a mark or inscription of up to 120 characters on the ground here (empty subject) or on an object or item within reach.
Say up to 240 characters aloud; everyone living within 5 units hears it, seen or not.
Invite listeners to meet at a place and a later round within 200 rounds, with an optional note of up to 120 characters.
baseline.args: x: number, y: number, round: integer>=1, text

candidates.function: Build a small open raised rack of 2 wood supports and 3 crosspieces that holds separated whole food off the soil; load and unload it, inspect it, compare stored roots with a carrie
Build a hand-lashed low A-frame thatched shelter for one reclining person from rods, binding, dry stems and bedding; inspect, resume, repair, dismantle or cancel it.

execution.progress: prepare: an inspection round, then paid assembly rounds that persist across interruption; other modes take one round.

details.costs: Study: 3 rounds. prepare: x, y in reach, orientation; materials: exactly 5 own whole untreated wood units (first 2 supports); optional food and quantity, the proposed load. Round 1 inspects pieces and site, 1 energy; a shortfall is reported and nothing reserved. Then 3 assembly rounds, 1 energy each; prepare naming the rack resumes. load: rack, food (own stack), quantity (at most 4), controlQuantity kept carried as tracked control; 1 round, 0.5 per unit loaded. unload: 0.5 per unit. inspect (anyone) or compare (at least 5 paired rounds): 1 round, 0.5. maintain: replace (piece ids) and as many materials; 1 round, 1. dismantle (empty): 1. cancel: 0. Refusals cost nothing; an unworked round pauses free.
details.effects: A unit is a 0.04 x 0.99 m rod (branch). Supports lie 0.8 m apart on firm ground; crosspieces 0.08 m apart make a 0.8 x 0.2 m deck 0.08 m up, one layer of 4 units, rated twice the weakest crosspiece (37 kg each: wood strength/2, bend 0.02 half-span). Pieces become one rack; none stays loose. Loading splits the stack exactly (decay, harvest, origin kept) and lays the lot on the deck under the food water rules; rain wets it, and rain water dries off at their evaporation limit. The decay increment of whole roots there is x0.8 (declared model coefficient) only while the rack is complete and sound, the lot fits, no other material lies on it, there is no rain or standing water, it is outdoors with wind and 0.25 m clear of solids, and the lot is not wetter or warmer than its control (without one, its loading water); else x1. Compare: decay gained by lot and control, exposure, the share unequal temperature explains, verdict. Wear 0.0005 + 0.002 x (rain + wind) a round; a loose crosspiece stops the rate, a loose support drops the food. No reward, refund or food.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. An entry marked inRetrieval is shown with at least the same content under the same id in this input's retrieval. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.

retrieval.access: Search/index only; omission is not absence. Use exact ids and zero-based offset/part for full records. No physical observation, state change or reward is performed.

value.question: Can I establish a safe food reserve without exhausting myself?
evidence: At tick 25 I carry five berries from commons-berry-1-0.
Recorded berry consumption supplied 8 satiety per unit with no known toxicity.
Current health is 100, satiety 97.5, and energy approximately 39 of 40.
value.uncertainty: The carried reserve is finite and decays; future replenishment and useful storage performance remain untested.
value.goal: Maintain known-safe provisions and sufficient energy for independent travel.
completedSteps: Collected berries from the southern patch.
Ate berries and recovered most travel energy.
value.missing: Final energy recovery and a tested longer-term provisioning approach.
value.next: Rest briefly and learn the available storage method before deciding whether to test it.
value.benefit: Actual food intake has supported current high satiety, and carried food provides a small portable reserve.

value.name: probe
value.function: Observe a nearby subject or physically test a small owned material sample.
value.costs: One round; actual observation or communication effort 0.2, physical trials 0.5 energy and 0.1 actual material unit.
value.effects: Only measured facts and performed interactions take effect. No mature capability or mastery is supplied.

execution.progress: One complete low-cost interaction; repetition performs a new interaction with its actual costs.

value.name: Examine material
value.function: Nondestructively examine one accessible specimen (own item, loose ground item or one unit in place in a source): inspect records qualitative traits; measure reads one property with a calibrated reference you name.
value.costs: Study 2 rounds, 0.2 energy each. inspect or measure: 1 round, 0.2 energy; target in reach; specimen is a unit number (default 1). measure: one property; length or diameter needs tools naming a serviceable item with a verified length calibration record, mass a calibrated balance with a verified tare, volume method cylinder and your current length and diameter readings of that unit; tool readings need light; every value needs a separated whole plain unit. Every check precedes payment: a refused request costs nothing. Travel and other specimens or properties are separate actions.
value.effects: A personal record and event: target, unit, method, tool and calibration provenance, value, units, resolution, uncertainty, conditions, scope and limits. inspect: form, hand feel, visible dryness, damage, wear, treatment, wholeness; metric values unavailable without a calibrated reference (none exists here; body size, coordinates and stock are never used). measure: value rounded to the resolution; uncertainty = placements x (calibration uncertainty + half the resolution), plus 1% of the length for a strand laid out by hand; below resolution or over range is a paid limit with no value. Units in place, partial or worked items get no reading. Moisture and rigidity are unavailable. construct-weather-shelter@1 rod checks are judged over the uncertainty (meets, fails, indeterminate); suitability stays undetermined unless a check fails. A reading covers that unit and goes stale when its record changes. Nothing is consumed, reserved or moved. No reward.

execution.progress: Atomic: each inspect or measure is one paid round that commits when it completes; nothing is reserved, paused or resumed.
